messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's batching split roll we saw a tail latency bump on the dedicated pool. p95 for decode-heavy flows jumped ~110ms while prefill p95 stayed flat. Anyone else observing KV eviction or kernel fallbacks?

kai: I noticed a smallbatch surge on canary around the same time. It looks like kernels are switching to the generic path a lot more when many tiny decode batches arrive. Suspect selector heuristics.

devin: grabbed a quick perf dump from the canary. flamegraph shows a new hot path in kernel_dispatch -> generic_attention. counters: kernel_switches +42% vs baseline. snippet:

```
# perf summary
generic_attention  42.1%
optimized_attn_v2  18.3%
kernel_select      12.4%
kv_cache_evict     9.7%
```

alex: That matches my theory — prefill and decode are contending for the same optimized kernels. When many tiny decodes hit, selector chooses generic to avoid waiting for batch shape, causing latency tail. Idea: pin decode batches to a lighter-weight kernel pool or strengthen token-budget gating so they coalesce.

sam: Quick config check — we had token_budget.decode removed in yesterday's patch (was 16 -> now unlimited). That would explain more tiny decode batches passing through. We set prefill to 64 earlier. Re-adding decode cap should reduce fragmentation.

lisa: ops-bot shows KV cache eviction spikes coincident with the tail. excerpt:

```
[2026-03-17T22:13:05Z] kv_cache::evict key_count=3120 evicted=124 window_ms=120
[2026-03-17T22:13:06Z] kv_cache::evict key_count=2984 evicted=200 window_ms=80
```

bench-bot: microbench run on canary -> p50 unchanged, p95 decode +120ms, prefill unaffected. QPS similar. lines:

- baseline: p95_decode=180ms
- canary: p95_decode=300ms

maria: To be pragmatic: propose quick A/B on the dedicated pool: 1) re-add token_budget.decode=8 (soft limit), 2) pin decode workloads to kernel_affinity=fast-math-v1, 3) enable kv_priming for 200ms for recurring sessions. Roll canary and observe for 15m.

kai: Also add a queue-manager tweak: if decode_queue_rate > 200r/s and avg_batch_size < 4, enable smallbatch_coalesce for 200ms. That should reduce selector churn.

devin: I pushed a minimal patch that reapplies the decode cap and sets the coalesce window. ran a short perf, p95 improved from 300ms -> 210ms. commit: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/commit/ab12c3f

alex: Nice. We should also instrument kernel_selector to emit a metric for 'fallthrough_select' (when optimized kernel skipped due to batch shape). That will help future tuning instead of guessing.

sam: Rolling the canary with the revert+coalesce now. Canary id: canary-2026-03-17-09. Will post metrics in ~10m.

lisa: Monitoring KV_hotset, kernel_switch_rate, decode_p95. ops-bot will alert on >10% kv_eviction increase.

ops-bot: canary canary-2026-03-17-09 deployed to 3 nodes at 4136007940. Health checks pass.

maria: If this stabilizes, we should follow up with a longer test: A) evaluate different decode token caps (4,8,16) B) measure cost delta when pinning kernels C) add selector metric as alex suggested. I'll draft a short runbook.

kai: Agreed. Also add a note to suggest KV priming TTL be proportional to session reuse rate; 200ms was arbitrary.

devin: I'll add the selector metric and a small histogram for batch sizes hitting each kernel. PR inbound.

sam: Canary metrics look promising: decode p95 down to ~205ms, kv_eviction down ~35%. Holding for 30m.

maria: Thanks all. Postmortem/notes later, but immediate action: keep decode cap in config until we do a controlled sweep. :)
